Q1

x <- c(NA, rnorm(n=20))
fivenum(x)
## [1] -2.3300706 -0.8189322 -0.5778432  0.3115180  1.4916261
fivenum(x)[4] - fivenum(x)[2]
## [1] 1.13045
f <- function(x) {
  return(fivenum(x)[4] - fivenum(x)[2])
}

y <- c(NA, rnorm(n=67))
z <- c(NA, rnorm(n=100))
f(x); f(y); f(z)
## [1] 1.13045
## [1] 1.551939
## [1] 1.516763
IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE); IQR(y, na.rm = TRUE); IQR(z, na.rm = TRUE)
## [1] 1.069988
## [1] 1.551939
## [1] 1.481569
CompHinge <- function(n) {
  x <- c(NA, rnorm(n = n))

  f(x) - IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

diff1<- replicate(1000, CompHinge(20))

diff2 <- replicate(1000, CompHinge(200))
diff3 <- replicate(1000, CompHinge(2000))
hist(diff1, main = "n = 20", xlab = "Hinge diff - IQR")

hist(diff2, main = "n = 200", xlab = "Hinge diff - IQR")

hist(diff3, main = "n = 2000", xlab = "Hinge diff - IQR")

  1. As the sample size n increased, the differences between the two functions approached 0, but the two functions aren’t perfectly identical

Q3

1 & 2.

set.seed(999)

x1 <- gl(2, 100)
x2 <- runif(200)

y <- c( rnorm(n = 100, mean = 20 - 0.5*x2[1:100], sd = 3),
  rnorm(n = 100, mean = 10 - 0.5*x2[101:200], sd = 3))
X <- model.matrix(y ~ x1 + x2)


beta_LS3 <- function(X, y) {
  solve(crossprod(X), crossprod(X, y))
  }

beta_hat <- beta_LS3(X, y)
beta_hat
##                    [,1]
## (Intercept)  19.2919320
## x12         -10.1748632
## x2            0.5335609
t1 <- crossprod(y) #all terms of numerator
t2 <- crossprod(y, X %*% beta_hat)
t3 <- crossprod(beta_hat, crossprod(X, y))
t4 <- crossprod(beta_hat, crossprod(X) %*% beta_hat)

(t1 - t2 - t3 + t4) / 197; anova(lm(y ~ x1 + x2))$"Mean Sq"[3]
##          [,1]
## [1,] 8.539789
## [1] 8.539789
mse <- anova(lm(y ~ x1 + x2))$"Mean Sq"[3]

H <- solve(crossprod(X)) * as.numeric(mse)

sqrt(diag(H)); sqrt(diag(vcov(lm(y ~ x1 + x2))))
## (Intercept)         x12          x2 
##   0.4555073   0.4132815   0.7171376
## (Intercept)         x12          x2 
##   0.4555073   0.4132815   0.7171376
y <- c(10, 9, 4, 5, 14, 20, 20, 19, 7)
x1 <- c(7, 3, 5, 0, 2, -6, -4, -6, -1)
x2 <- c(-4, -1, -1, 4, 6, 1, 0, -5, 0)

X <- model.matrix(y ~ x1 + x2)
XtX <- crossprod(X)
XtX
##             (Intercept)  x1 x2
## (Intercept)           9   0  0
## x1                    0 176  0
## x2                    0   0 96
XtXi <- solve(XtX)
XtXi
##             (Intercept)          x1         x2
## (Intercept)   0.1111111 0.000000000 0.00000000
## x1            0.0000000 0.005681818 0.00000000
## x2            0.0000000 0.000000000 0.01041667
beta_LS4 <- function(X, y) {
  crossprod(X, y) / diag(crossprod(X))
}

beta_LS3(X, y); beta_LS4(X, y)
##              [,1]
## (Intercept) 12.00
## x1          -1.00
## x2          -0.25
##              [,1]
## (Intercept) 12.00
## x1          -1.00
## x2          -0.25
library(microbenchmark)

microbenchmark(
  beta_LS3 = beta_LS3(X, y),
  beta_LS4 = beta_LS4(X, y),
  times = 1000)
## Unit: microseconds
##      expr    min      lq     mean  median      uq      max neval
##  beta_LS3 14.833 15.8830 52.22354 16.4270 17.3800 14061.66  1000
##  beta_LS4 12.190 13.4375 50.59286 14.0535 15.0485 30471.96  1000

Q4

e4 <- runif(10000)

csum <- function(x) {
  if(length(x) == 1) return(x)
  
  sumx <- x[1]
  for(i in seq(2, length(x))) {
    sumx[i] <- sum(x[1:i])
  }
  sumx
}

out <- csum(e4)
all.equal(out, cumsum(e4))
## [1] TRUE

The function sum() is repeated inside the loop for every single iteration of the for loop x[1:i] repeatedly calls a vector that’s constantly increasing Calculating basically the same sum over and over again takes up too much time

csum2 <- function(x) {
  if(length(x) == 1) return(x)
  
  sumx <- numeric(length(x)) 
  # create blank vector with same length ONCE to use 

  temp <- x[1]
  sumx[1] <- temp

  #add ONE new value at each iteration
  for (i in seq(2, length(x))) {
    temp <- temp + x[i]
    sumx[i] <- temp
  }
  sumx
}

out <- csum2(e4)
all.equal(out, cumsum(e4))
## [1] TRUE
 time <- microbenchmark(csum = csum(e4),
                csum2 = csum2(e4),
                cumsum = cumsum(e4),times = 10)

time2 <- summary(time)
time2
##     expr        min         lq        mean      median         uq        max
## 1   csum 244598.844 246038.972 273055.8262 284430.9745 285724.389 310051.459
## 2  csum2    629.027    640.603    720.6328    701.3480    787.481    891.088
## 3 cumsum     10.199     10.861     12.9943     11.7395     15.833     17.902
##   neval
## 1    10
## 2    10
## 3    10
((time2$median[1] - time2$median[2])/time2$median[1]) * 100
## [1] 99.75342

csum2() takes 99.8% less time to execute

How many evaluations of cumsum() can be performed per second?

cumsum_median <- time2$median[time2$expr == "cumsum"]

1 / (cumsum_median * 1e-6)
## [1] 85182.5
